text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "The essay consistently spells complex words correctly (e.g., \"alleviate\", \"overwhelmed\", \"experienced\", \"distractions\"), unlike Essay A's errors such as \"bad wives\" for \"bad vibes\".", "quality": "Spelling Accuracy", "description": "This quality captures a writer's ability to spell words correctly throughout the essay without phonetically misspelled errors."}, {"evidence": "The writer consistently maintains correct subject-verb agreement and complex clause structures (e.g., \"By asking multiple people, you can get multiple ideas\"), whereas Essay A uses nonstandard forms like \"I'm agree\" and \"positively brings resilient\".", "quality": "Grammatical Control", "description": "This quality reflects the student's mastery over standard English syntax and grammatical rules."}, {"evidence": "The writer structures the response into well-organized paragraphs introduced by clear topic sentences (\"One way seeking multiple opinions...\", \"Another way...\", \"A final way...\") that systematically build the thesis.", "quality": "Paragraph Organization and Coherence", "description": "This quality measures how effectively a text uses structural markers and logical paragraph divisions to guide the reader through a multi-point argument."}]}
